input: search for a specific word inside a file
find a word in a file
look for a word in a file

arguments.command:
tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Please enter the word to find" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
🔍 Word to find: " && read -r word && if [ -n "$word" ]; then termy_say "Please enter the target file path" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "📄 Target file: " && read -r targetfile && if [ -f "$targetfile" ]; then printf "
Matches for \033[1m%s\033[22m:
" "$word" && grep -n "$word" "$targetfile" && printf "
" && termy_say "Search completed" > /dev/null 2>&1; else printf "
⛔ Target file does not exist.
" && termy_say "File not found" > /dev/null 2>&1; fi; else printf "

" && termy_say "Operation cancelled" > /dev/null 2>&1; fi

input: compress a directory into an archive
create an archive from a directory
create zip or tar from a directory

arguments.command:
tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Please enter the directory to compress" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
📁 Directory to compress: " && read -r source_dir && if [ -d "$source_dir" ]; then termy_say "Please choose an archive format" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
1) TAR.GZ - Linux standard
2) ZIP - Cross platform

Choose format 1-2: " && read -r arch_choice; case "$arch_choice" in 1) tar -czf "$source_dir.tar.gz" "$source_dir" && printf "
Archive \033[1m%s.tar.gz\033[22m created.
" "$source_dir" && termy_say "Archive created successfully" > /dev/null 2>&1 ;; 2) zip -r "$source_dir.zip" "$source_dir" && printf "
Archive \033[1m%s.zip\033[22m created.
" "$source_dir" && termy_say "Archive created successfully" > /dev/null 2>&1 ;; *) printf "
⛔ Invalid choice.
" && termy_say "Invalid selection" > /dev/null 2>&1 ;; esac; else printf "
⛔ Directory does not exist.
" && termy_say "Directory not found" > /dev/null 2>&1; fi
arguments.explanation: Compresses a directory into either a TAR.GZ or ZIP archive based on user choice.
